The stop-gain transcript is NMD-targeted: 748 nt from PTC (CDS 2209) to the last exon junction (CDS 2957), six downstream junctions (2284..2957), exon 17/23, 698 nt past the 50-nt rule; context TGAA

openFDA label for hydroxychloroquine sulfate states safety and effectiveness ESTABLISHED in pediatric patients for malaria treatment and prophylaxis; the same label limits the film-coated tablets to children of at least 31 kg because they cannot be crushed or divided
No ingredient ranks in the top 100 of all three screen lanes simultaneously

Verdict updates: hydroxychloroquine class promoted (Tang 2011 aneuploidy-selective vulnerability + established pediatric malaria label, with the >=31 kg tablet restriction narrowing the pediatric leg); metformin demoted (weak subordinate Tang 2011 evidence); NMN is best biological but status-blocked (in-vivo BubR1 raise in wild-type mice, North 2014; lawful dietary supplement since FDA's 2025-09-29 reversal of the 2022 exclusion, still not an FDA-approved medication); amlexanox unchanged bench-only (exposure gap ~10x); fostamatinib rejected as screen-flag-only (background-level LINCS read on a validation-limited lane)
Ataluren EU authorization ended 2025-03-28 after efficacy unconfirmed; amlexanox exposure vs potency gap ~5 uM serum vs >=50 uM effective
